title: Sensation is the pickup, and perception is the reading of it
summary: Sensation happens when a receptor detects a stimulus, and perception is how that information is organized, interpreted, and consciously experienced.
body: OpenStax Psychology says sensation has occurred when a sensory receptor detects sensory information. The conversion of stimulus energy into a nerve signal is transduction. Perception is the way sensory information is organized, interpreted, and consciously experienced. The chapter says sensation is a physical process and perception is psychological. Not every sensation becomes a perception. The text is CC BY 4.0.

sources.title: 5.1 Sensation versus Perception
sources.author: OpenStax
sources.note: OpenStax Psychology, first edition, section 5.1, CC BY 4.0. No revision date was printed on the page. Supports the distinction: sensation as receptor detection, perception as organization, interpretation, and conscious experience.
